messages:
alexa: Heads-upwe're seeing intermittent p95 tails (~20ms) on a handful of GPU hosts in rack r45 when tenant-77 runs lots of short LLM calls. Baseline idle otherwise. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/cluster/r45

ops-bot: [Alert] egress-p95-elevated on r45 (04:12 UTC). Runbook link: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/egress-noise

dmitri: Any signs of NIC saturation vs softirq imbalance? Small packets + high pps can blow out coalescing and qdisc head-of-line.

alexa: Quick host dump from r45-node3:
```
eth0 tx_queue_len: 52
p95_rtt_ms: 19.7
irq_rate_pps: 110000
softirq_skew: cpu3
top_tx_owner: tenant-77-sidecar:8080 (pid 5123)
```

yasmin: This reads like a telemetry/sidecar pps storm starving control RPCs. Low CPU but huge pps on single core. Two low-friction mitigations: 1) spread IRQs across cores, 2) throttle sidecar egress with tc for that cgroup. Longer-term: jitter polling in telemetry and auto-attribution on alerts.

dmitri: Agreed. We should try irq spread first (no customer impact). If that reduces tail but not enough, apply per-tenant policing and then consider shifting tenant to a tiny dedicated slice if it keeps recurring.

ops-bot: Applying irq-affinity-spread to r45-node[2-4] now.

alexa: After irq spread p95 -> 8.3ms, tx_queue_len -> 19. Improvement but still above baseline (~3ms).

yasmin: Let's enable a short per-tenant egress throttle: 80mbit burst 8ms on tenant-77 cgroup for immediate relief. I'll run as a canary on node3.

dmitri: If that stabilizes we add the throttle play to the runbook. Also add ticket to estimate cost of tiny dedicated slices (owner: pete) and a probe that attributes alerts to top-sender-cgroup.

ops-bot: Per-tenant egress policing applied (04:28 UTC) on node3.

alexa: After policing p95 back to 3.4ms on node3. Rolling watch for 30m.

pete: I'll run cost calc for tiny dedicated carveouts and post numbers in INFRA-2100. Preliminary note: carving a single-tenant tiny-slice for isolation is roughly 2x the marginal cost for that tenant during peak due to reservation headroom and replication overhead. Exact depends on slice size and region.

yasmin: Nice. Follow-ups: (1) add jitter to telemetry defaults (yasmin), (2) add auto-attribution field to egress alerts (dmitri), (3) add carveout cost appendix to runbook (pete). I'll update runbook with the short play: irq-spread -> 3m wait -> per-tenant policing -> consider tiny-slice.

alexa: Thanks team. Leaving monitors on and will file traces + tcpdumps into INFRA-2100. :white_check_mark:
